text:
For most camping, a **205–300Wh-class unit** is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, camera batteries, and a CPAP for a few nights. For longer trips or a fridge, step up to about 1kWh.

## Best picks by trip type

**Weekend camping (phones, lights, CPAP)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**: 288Wh, 300W AC, about 8.3 lb, around $249. Our top pick for simplicity and portability. Jackery's own site no longer lists it, though it's still sold through Amazon and other retailers, and a newer Explorer 300 v2 has replaced it with a shorter warranty. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**: 286Wh with a 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh, about $269–299. Best value if you run heavier gear. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Anker SOLIX C300**: 288Wh, about $199, with a retractable lantern and a 5-year warranty. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Bluetti EB3A**: 268Wh, 600W, about $179 on sale. The budget choice. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))

**Longer trips, small fridge, or van life**
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: 890Wh measured, about 25 lb, 1,800W, six AC outlets. Tested at about $530 on sale. It's noisy under load. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: 1,070Wh, about 24 lb, 1,500W, around $799. TechRadar lists it as a top camping pick. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Bluetti AC180**: 1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb (16 kg), with 4 AC outlets and a 5-year warranty. Listed at $499 on the official store, and the source reports a code (AFF5OFF) that took $24.95 off when tested on 2026-10-21. Checkout has the final word. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))
  - Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180
  - **Disclosure:** that page is an affiliate link. Dealectric earns a commission if you buy, and the page's own coupon testing is funded by it.

**Multi-day off-grid or extended blackouts**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: 1,710Wh usable, 2,200W, about 39 lb, and it's OutdoorGearLab's top off-grid pick. Listed at $1,499 but recently under $900 on Amazon. It can't run a space heater for long. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: 1,536Wh, IP65 rated, about 40 lb, with a comfortable handle. WIRED's pick for camping, at about $1,079 on Amazon. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))

## Where to buy

My search results didn't include direct retailer product links, so these are Amazon searches you can use to find current listings:
- [Jackery Explorer 300 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+300+Plus)
- [EcoFlow River 3 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=EcoFlow+River+3+Plus)
- [Anker SOLIX C300](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C300)
- [Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C1000+Gen+2)
- [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+1000+v2)

Prices in these sources are dated, and some are sale prices that change often. Confirm the current price at checkout.

## My suggestion

For a typical weekend, get the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** or the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**. If you want a fridge or multi-night trips, get the **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** or the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**. Tell me your trip length and what you plan to run, and I can narrow this down.
